title: Understanding the Structure and Dynamics of Peptide-Based Coacervates with In-Situ Liquid and Cryo-TEM
content: The formation and evolution of coacervates have significant implications in fields ranging from biomaterials to cellular organization. Coacervates are dynamic liquid droplets that undergo phase separation from bulk aqueous solution, with interesting structural and functional properties. Although droplets formed via liquid liquid phase separation have been extensively studied at the micron level with optical microscopy [1], understanding the structural details of the molecules that assemble into these liquid droplets in their native environment, and characterizing their nanoscale dynamics simultaneously presents a significant challenge. Here we report valuable insights into the morphological evolution of peptide-based coacervates in liquid with nanometer resolution, under different formation mechanisms using liquid phase transmission electron microscopy (LPTEM). The structural details derived from our LPTEM observations were further confirmed through cryogenic transmission electron microscopy (Cryo-TEM).
